# Excellence 2026: Resident Experience Solutions in Action


November 02, 2026


by Craig Patton


##


People experience government through the services and interactions that shape everyday life — reporting a pothole, doing business with a city, accessing information, or depending on public agencies when circumstances are urgent. Increasingly, residents and businesses expect those interactions to be simple, responsive, and transparent.


Technology can help government meet those expectations by connecting people with services, giving them greater visibility into processes, and helping public-sector employees respond more effectively. A better resident experience isn’t limited to what happens on a screen. It is reflected in how easily people can engage with government, how reliably services are delivered, and how those interactions build trust.


## Celebrating Excellence in Resident Experience Solutions


For 2027, the[Tyler Excellence Awards](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards) are introducing a Resident Experience category to recognize organizations using technology to foster trust, simplify interactions, and strengthen engagement with residents and the business community. While the category is new, Tyler clients were already demonstrating these outcomes in their 2026 award-winning stories across other categories. The examples below show how technology can improve everyday services, support local businesses, and help agencies respond when needs are urgent.


## Connecting Service Requests for Greater Transparency


Managing facilities, infrastructure, fleets, schools, and parks across the city siloed asset data for the city of Lowell, Massachusetts. The city implemented Enterprise Asset Management integrated with Enterprise ERP and Enterprise Service Requests in a unified platform for work orders, asset condition tracking, preventative maintenance, and performance insight. The city:


- Improved transparency and coordination across departments
- Enabled data-driven decisions
- Extended asset life, improving taxpayer value


## Bringing Court Services Closer to the Community


[Victoria Municipal Court](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/blog-articles/texas-court-models-justice-around-people-resolves-more-cases) developed an expanded docketing strategy to meet people where they are after experiencing increased failure-to-appears. Through creative use of their case management system, the court:


- Increased access to services through weekend, night, and virtual availability, improving public perception
- Expedited case resolution with less reliance on paper
- Helped the public clear records faster with payment plans, reduced fines, and community service options


“There are clear barriers to justice, but we’ve addressed them using capabilities of our existing technology,” said Judge Heinold. “We’re handling cases more effectively now — the way our community deserves.”


## Accelerating Response When Every Minute Matters


Often involving multiple agencies and several hours of work,[Pinellas County, Florida](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/pinellas-county-pioneers-safety-digitizes-protection-orders) , aimed to process risk protection orders more efficiently. Since implementing CloudGavel, they have:


- Connected law enforcement and judicial officials through electronic document routing
- Reduced processing times from 2-3 hours to 5-10 minutes, resulting in more processed orders than in years past
- Increased public and law enforcement safety through electronic efficiency gains and expanded access


“The fact that we can do it so quickly and seamlessly, it frees up resources that would have been tied up for hours or days,” said Olivier Lindemann, former associate counsel for the Pinellas County Sheriff’s Office.


More TEA Winners: Explore the rest of the[2026 Tyler Excellence Award winners](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards/2026-winners) and their stories across every category. As applications open for 2027, the new Resident Experience category will recognize organizations designing better civic experiences through technology that strengthens trust and makes interactions with government simpler and more responsive.


2026 Award Categories: Lowell, Massachusetts — Civic Interaction & Public Trust; Victoria Municipal Court, Texas — Performance & Innovation; Pinellas County, Florida — Digital Services & Cloud.
